description: Reinterpret row-pair inner products as syndromes and borrow decoder architectures from topological quantum memories. An auxiliary CA propagates defect messages across overlapping row neighborhoods, attempting local pairing and cancellation before an exact verifier decides whether the update helped.
mathematical_formalization: Let S = {(i,j) : D_ij != 0} for D_ij = <H_i, H_j>. Build a factor graph whose variables are row bits and whose checks are pairwise orthogonality constraints. A decoder CA maintains messages m_t and selects local flips F_t = psi(m_t, D_t) so that syndrome weight ||D_t||_0 or energy sum D_ij^2 falls.
analogical_connections: Stabilizer neighborhoods turned into row-overlap neighborhoods.
Local decoding instead of global matrix search.
implementation_hypothesis: Construct a sparse message graph from block interactions, adapt a local decoder rule to pass defect messages, and test whether message-guided flips outperform direct local repair.
experiment_seed: Inject controlled defects into exact smaller Hadamards and measure syndrome collapse speed, then apply the same decoder to modular-seed residuals.

closest_prior_art.title: Cellular-automaton decoders for topological quantum memories
A Quantum Approximate Optimization Method For Finding Hadamard Matrices

novelty_claim: This is a decoder-style CA for Gram-defect fields, not a generic search heuristic and not a direct translation of a quantum-code decoder.
differentiation: The target checks are dense orthogonality constraints compressed into a structured factor graph, which is a different object from the sparse stabilizer graphs used in prior decoder work.
